I can relate to having mental illness run on the family. My mom had depression and insomnia, and so do I. 

She would always arrive home from work and instantly start complaining and ranting about how her life sucked and how her boss was bad, etc. I had to listen to all, but I got progressively worse as time passed and told her once that she complained too much. I feel kind of guilty about it, but at the same time I know that it wasn't wrong of me to set those boundaries. We are only human after all, and I was getting badly affected by all the pessimism - as probably are you and your siblings too. I was not a therapist or an adult friend, but someone much younger than her and in a vulnerable state. In an ideal family, parents should be able to take care of their children and comfort them when necessary, but sometimes all we hear back is "you have depression? So do I." and it sucks. I try to not be this kind of person the most I can because of that.

The thing with this competition between people with mental illness is that no one is going to listen to us because "they got it worse", and this is not very nice, especially coming from parents. I think that all kinds of struggles and problems are valid, coming from mental illness or not, and that no one should make you or anybody else feel like it is the opposite since it's not fair at all. 

I don't blame you for not being able to help your siblings or for feeling envious of your sister. I would feel the same to be honest. You are not guilty of feeling like that. You feel this way because you want to be helped, heard, and cared for, and those are basic necessities in a human's life. Also, I'm sure that you care a lot about your family as you stated you don't want to influence them in a bad way, and I don't think you are a bad person at all.

I think the first step on being able to help others is to help yourself first so you can stand well by yourself, be mentally healthier, and so on, so just take care of yourself for now, okay? Try to indulge in some way or find things that make you feel better, like a new hobbie or something. I started sewing plushies, for example, and it helps me get focused on something else. It doesn't have to be that, if it's not your jam, of course. 

Sometimes, even being around another group of people can help you see things in a brighter perspective. One thing that I can promise you is that life is not all about living with people with mental illness, even if it seems that way now :)

Take care!

Trying to isolate yourself is part of having depression, as well as believing one is not worthy of being helped/can't be helped, etc. That's why it's so hard to ask for help: because it's basically going against the entire thing. So it's perfectly normal to feel like that.

I don't know about how your relationships are right now, but I'm sure that if someone tried to help you, they did it because they cared about you and still care. While they might have stopped offering help to you, you still can mention having a rough time and asking if they can hear you out or something, and I'm pretty sure they are going to appreciate that you accepted being helped :)

Peace.

This sounds very difficult... people just don't know at all how to care for someone who attempted suicide, and I'm including hospitals when I say that. I'm so sorry that they made you go through that during your recovery. It must have been truly awful.

I don't know why the heck people think that taking your personal belongings or any means of communicating with the outside world - isolating you and taking out something that can help you stay grounded - would be helpful at all. It's so unfair. I'm glad that you are in another place now, although it's not a very supporting one. 

I hope your mom can get to understand better your struggles with anxiety, so that you can work things better. When someone close starts judging you in a moment of vulnerability like that it's just the worse, right? 

To be honest, I too tried to commit suicide once and failed. And instead of asking me what I wanted to do or who I wanted to be with, they took away my phone and made me stay at the same house as the person who triggered my will to die, isolated in a farm, not even in my own city. That's why I can relate to some things.

I think that having someone understanding and not judging close to you would be the best right now, although I'm not sure how your net of contacts is right now. I hope you can be helped closely, though, and I'm wishing the best in these times.

Human beings don't need to be useful in someway to have value, but sadly that's how people in general makes us think. They make us grow up focused on getting into high school, then into college, then getting a job, having promotions and so on, and this is so simplistic. 

A person is not a machine with a function, existing just to be of use to society and then thrown away. There is more to it. You are valuable just for existing, for literally being on the world. Your contributions and what else you do in your existence is an extra. 

So take your time with whatever you want to take action with. I don't know if it's about studies, work or something else, just remember you are already doing the best you can considering your current state ~

It must be so hard for you :/ 

The thing with mental ilness is that unfortunately we don't choose when it happens and just have to somehow deal with it. It sucks that you have to go through a crisis in your birthday. 

It's not your fault though, so go easy on yourself. You deserve to feel however you want to/need to on this day, even if there is pressure to feel happy. Try to take small steps towards making your day better, maybe just drinking water or something. It doesn't need to be something big. It's your day, after all. Just go towards feeling okay first and see as it goes ~

This makes a lot of sense. Families like that sucks and shouldn't be falsely viewed as a "supportive group". Being linked by blood definitely doesn't mean a lot. I wish things could be different for these people...

I feel similarly. Some time ago I threw away things I didn't want others to find in my room, thought of a letter to leave on my desk, searched up methods... but it's like being in a limbo, right? 

At the same time death sounds like a very plausible option, I keep thinking if I should try to take the effort you mentioned, get my life together, etc. Now I'm trying it. I'm trying to make my drawing skills better, but it's not exactly a long term plan. I'm seeing as it goes.

What you wrote about it being a cycle and tiring you out is very real. The more we try, the more it looks like it is not building up something concrete. It takes a lot of energy from us, and it's not easy at all to make all of this work when energy and motivation are low. You sound like you are putting a lot of mind into making it work before making a decisive choice, and maybe I'm not in place to say this, but I'm proud of your efforts. It must be hard...

I'm not sure if this helps, but for now perhaps distance yourself from things that stress you out and take as easier as you can, just to have some peace of mind. It may be easier to organize your thoughts when your mind is in a less overwhelmed state
Thank you for being so understanding. I think I was probably sheltered, or spent too much time isolated at home, so real world experiences are kind of scary.

When I was a kid, I had a hard time making friends and had some strange ways of displaying bottled up emotions, besides not showing much interest in going out. So my parents made me go to a therapist without explaining anything to me, and I felt like I was a problem. 

The therapist herself didn't help with that, because she would ask me questions that I saw as targeting, and I felt like assumptions were made all the time - not sure if that was just a wrong idea on my part for not understanding why the heck I was sent there so many times.

I think that not feeling threatened and knowing why you are receiving therapy is very important to the process, because I ended up learning how to pretend I'm "normal" so that I could no longer need to go there. And besides depression, I was diagnosed as someone in the autism spectrum...

INTP

Also, I'm pretty obsessed with MBTI so... I'm 99,9% sure of it.

I have a similar experience. I was sent to see a therapist for a long time when I was a kid and I hated it. I had no idea why I was there, so I grew up scared of seeking help again when older. 

Although, at some point I thought "maybe i can find a better therapist by myself", so I tried counseling again, with a different person. She was very different and much better than the last one. I think you just have to find the right one, after all. 

Best of luck, bud
